explanation: The October 30 document contains multiple substantive elements: a 25bp rate cut to 1.5-1.75%, a formal directive to purchase Treasury bills 'at least into the second quarter of next year' and conduct repo operations 'at least through January' — effectively announcing a balance sheet expansion program — and a notable forward guidance shift removing the 'act as appropriate' easing bias language, signaling a pause after three consecutive cuts. The October 11 announcement (referenced within the document) of the T-bill purchase program and repo operations to maintain reserves above early-September levels would itself constitute a between-meeting policy action that could explain a structural break around October 16.
